title: Naming what a slider leaves alone
question: How close could Hazel get to evaluating only what a slider change touches? ^report(10)'s question asked of every slider on three Livelit Playground slides, and of how the answer depends on how the calls are named, taking the design space of names from the merge sort in Fumola, where one computation is named three ways.

builds.name: measuring build
builds.note: with ^report(10)'s oracle extended on a local branch, not pushed: the reads of each call (variable lookups and callee results), a localized and an operand name for each call, and names told apart by order

fumola: the worked example, not measured here: Fumola's merge sort (levelTree.fumola) and its notes on naming, at commit 667a34d5f2
runtime: node, the test build. Versions not stated in the report.
programs: the Livelit Playground's Full Body, Witch and Scenes slides, each cut at its picture as in ^report(10)
edits: every Drawing.^slider on the three slides, 63 in all, found by its let's name; its model is the literal the slider's outer call is applied to. Each moved by a fifth of its range (down, if up would leave the range), with its literal's id kept, as a slider's commit keeps it. Each edit's slider, label, old and new value are in its ladder line.
runs: Each slide analyzed with Statics.mk_unmemoized and evaluated with Evaluator.evaluate once before the edits, again with no edit (the control, from scratch and incrementally), and twice for each edit: from scratch, and incrementally against the first run's cache, as the eval worker does. Every call of the two runs after the edit compared with the run before. Steps are deterministic, so one run of each suffices; every control is clean (the same program evaluated twice matches every call under every name, once names that would collide are told apart by their order). Two further runs: the eye-size and eye-gap edits on Full Body and Witch again, with every call's variables recorded (the diagnosis), and three Full Body sliders moved by one instead of a fifth.

measures.picture diff: % (or count of shapes): the shapes of the picture the edit changed, as a share of the picture's shapes, found by comparing the two pictures shape by shape (as in ^report(10)). A diff of the result, not of the computation; it counts shapes, not steps. Edits that change how many shapes there are have none (printed 'B -> A shapes').
measures.trace distance: % of a run from scratch: the fewest steps any update could evaluate again, under the best matching of the new run's trace to the old one's (in the sense of Acar and colleagues' work on self-adjusting computation). It belongs to the program and the edit, not to any cache. Estimated from above, by matching whole calls by their content (any call before with the same code and the same inputs), and more finely by matching each call's own steps by what it reads.
measures.update cost: % of a run from scratch: the steps an actual update evaluates again, given its cache, how its cache names what it keeps, and how it decides what to evaluate again: the steps of Hazel's incremental run today less what a memo of calls keyed by the scheme could skip, over the steps of the edited program evaluated from scratch. Never below the trace distance.
measures.Hazel's update, steps: count: the steps of Hazel's incremental run after the edit (it caches top-level bindings by the editor's ids)
measures.naming schemes: by position (the call path and a count, ^report(10)'s; 'path' in the raw files), by the caller (the caller's site and inputs, made unique by order; 'local'), by operand (the call site and the argument's value, made unique by order; 'operand'), by content (the call's code and every input)
measures.outcomes: count of calls after the edit, under a scheme: equal (a call before had its name and the same inputs), notEqual (its name, other inputs), onlyRight (a name new to this run); onlyLeft counts the calls before whose name is gone
measures.collisions: count: calls in one run sharing a name with an earlier call under a scheme, before names are told apart by order (Full Body: 1,375 by operand, 609 by caller)
measures.reads: steps: an update that matches each call's own steps by what it reads (every variable its own steps look up and the result of every call it makes, each with the hash of its value): a call whose reads all saw what the call of its name saw before skips its own steps
measures.cells: steps, an upper bound: as reads, with every list a call reads compared by its head alone, the rest stood in for by a name
measures.shapes changed, moved, scaled, rotated,: count (Figure 5): each changed shape compared with its old self: moved (every point translated alike), scaled (and maybe moved), rotated (and maybe scaled and moved), each one transform of the shape's old points; or reshaped, its geometry itself changed (the table's reshaped column includes shapes whose style alone changed)
measures.distinct transforms, nodes changed with: count: the distinct transforms among the changed shapes, and the nodes that would change in a picture of groups with transforms, at best: one per distinct transform plus one per shape reshaped or restyled
measures.functions that run again (eye sliders): for the eye-size and eye-gap edits, by position: each function whose calls run again, its calls, its own steps, and the variables whose values differ most often among those calls

table_notes: The four tables under #eyes have the same columns and no caption; the paragraph above each names it. In order: Full Body, eye size; Full Body, eye gap; Witch, eye size; Witch, eye gap. Each lists the eight functions with the most own steps among the calls that run again, by position.
times: not timed: counts of evaluation steps, not times, from an oracle that watches and reuses nothing, with every check free

raw_files.data/ladder011.output: The ladder: one tab-separated LADDER line per edit, and a CONTROL line per slide (66 lines; Scenes, then Full Body, then Witch). Fields: 'LADDER <slide>', the slider's name, its label, the old value, the new value, 'shapes <before> <after> same <n>' (n: shapes equal in place; -1 when the count changes), then 'SCRATCH' and the edited program evaluated from scratch, then 'TODAY' and it evaluated incrementally against the first run's cache. Each run: 'executed E in_calls C calls N content K' (K: the steps of the outermost calls matched by content) and one field per scheme, path, local and operand: '<scheme> skip S reads R cells L | equal a notEqual b onlyLeft c onlyRight d collisions e' (S: the steps of the outermost calls a memo keyed by the scheme could skip; R, L: the steps saved matching own steps by reads, and by reads with lists as named cells; then the four outcomes and the collisions). An update's cost is the TODAY run's E less what it saves (S, R, L or K), over the SCRATCH run's E. The sweep table, Figures 1 to 4 and the numbers in the text are from this file.
raw_files.data/diag011.output: The eye sliders' diagnosis: a run with every call's variables recorded, of the eye-size and eye-gap edits on Full Body and Witch, with each slide's control, as LADDER lines (as above), and tab-separated DIAG lines: 'DIAG <slide> <slider>', the function, '<n> calls', '<n> own steps', and 'differing:' the variables whose values differ most often among its calls, with counts (up to twelve functions an edit, by own steps; the report's tables show eight).
raw_files.data/representation011.json: Figure 5 and the representation table: a JSON list, one entry per edit, {slide, name, shapes, changed, kinds: {moved, scaled, rotated, reshaped, style}, transforms, tree, structural}: the shapes the edit changed, classified (above), the distinct transforms among them, and 'tree', the nodes that would change in a picture of groups with transforms, at best. An edit that changes how many shapes there are has structural true, and the shape counts before and after instead. Made by a script from the exported picture of every edit (68 JSON files, about 5.5 MB, not kept here).
raw_files.data/small_steps011.output: Three Full Body sliders moved by one instead (shirt width 66 -> 67, arm length 95 -> 96, hand size 14 -> 15), with the control, as LADDER lines: the source of 'moved by one instead, Full Body's shirt width, arm length and hand size change the same 39, 30 and 24 of its 49 shapes'.

provenance.dated notes: The notes added later on 2026-10-13 that point to ^report(12) (at most 14 nodes, the tree flattened is today's picture) are that report's measurements (012/data/).
provenance.Fumola: The Fumola section reports no measurements; its claims about pathwise, inductive and cartesian names are from Fumola's notes at commit 667a34d5f2.
